title: 08. Files & Errors: 03 — File Handling: Text, JSON, CSV, Binary, Pathlib (Deep Dive)
summary: Format chars: b/B byte, h/H short, i/I int, q/Q long long, f float, d double, s string. Prefix big-endian.

sections.title: 1. The open() builtin
sections.body:
```python
open(file, mode="r", buffering=-1, encoding=None, errors=None, newline=None, closefd=True, opener=None)
```

Modes (combine letters):

- `r` read (default), `w` write (truncate), `a` append, `x` exclusive create (fail if exists).
- `b` binary, `t` text (default).
- `+` read+write (e.g., `r+`, `w+`).

Best practices:

- **Always use `with`** — guarantees close even on exception.
- **Always pass `encoding="utf-8"`** for text — defaults differ on Windows (cp1252) vs Linux (utf-8).
- **`errors=` for handling bad bytes**: `"strict"` (default), `"ignore"`, `"replace"`, `"backslashreplace"`.

```python
with open("a.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
    data = f.read()
```

### Buffering

- `0` — unbuffered (binary only).
- `1` — line-buffered (text).
- `>1` — fixed buffer size in bytes.
- `-1` — system default (typically 8 KB).

sections.title: 2. Read & write methods
sections.body:
### Read

- `f.read()` — entire file as string. Don't on huge files.
- `f.read(n)` — up to n chars/bytes.
- `f.readline()` — one line including `\n`.
- `f.readlines()` — list of all lines (loads full file).
- `for line in f:` — memory-efficient streaming (preferred).

### Write

- `f.write(s)` — returns chars written, NO automatic newline.
- `f.writelines(iter)` — iterable of strings, NO newlines added.
- `print(..., file=f)` — convenient + auto newline.

### Position

- `f.tell()` — current position.
- `f.seek(offset, whence)` — `whence`: 0 start, 1 current, 2 end (binary only for ≠0).
- `f.flush()` — push buffer to OS (still not on disk).
- `os.fsync(f.fileno())` — force OS to flush to disk.

sections.title: 3. Text files — gotchas
sections.body:
- Line endings: Windows uses `\r\n`, Unix `\n`. In text mode Python translates automatically.
- For CSV use `newline=""` to disable translation (csv module handles it).
- Encoding errors → `UnicodeDecodeError`. Specify encoding always.
- BOM (Byte Order Mark): use `encoding="utf-8-sig"` to strip it on read.

sections.title: 4. JSON
sections.body:
```python
import json
# load
data = json.load(f)              # from file
data = json.loads(s)             # from string
# dump
json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str, sort_keys=False)
s = json.dumps(data)
```

Key options:

- `indent=2` — pretty-print.
- `ensure_ascii=False` — keep Unicode characters literal.
- `default=callable` — fallback for non-serializable objects.
- `sort_keys=True` — deterministic output.
- `separators=(",", ":")` — compact output.

### Custom encoder

```python
class MyEnc(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, o):
        import datetime, decimal
        if isinstance(o, (datetime.datetime, datetime.date)): return o.isoformat()
        if isinstance(o, decimal.Decimal): return str(o)
        if isinstance(o, set): return sorted(o)
        return super().default(o)

json.dumps(data, cls=MyEnc)
```

### Custom decoder via `object_hook`

```python
def hook(d):
    if "__dt__" in d: return datetime.fromisoformat(d["__dt__"])
    return d
json.loads(s, object_hook=hook)
```

### Streaming huge JSON

- Use `ijson` (3rd party) for SAX-like parsing.
- Or use **JSON Lines** (`.jsonl`): one object per line, trivially streamable.

```python
with open("data.jsonl") as f:
    for line in f:
        obj = json.loads(line)
```

### Security

- `json.loads` is safe by default (no code execution).
- `eval`/`pickle.loads` on untrusted input = remote code execution.

sections.title: 5. CSV
sections.body:
```python
import csv

# read with reader (rows are lists)
with open("d.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f, delimiter=",", quotechar='"')
    headers = next(reader)
    for row in reader: ...

# read with DictReader (rows are dicts)
with open("d.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        print(row["name"])

# write
with open("o.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["name", "age"])
    w.writeheader()
    w.writerow({"name": "A", "age": 30})
    w.writerows([{...}, {...}])
```

Critical:

- `newline=""` is **mandatory** or you get blank rows on Windows.
- `quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL | QUOTE_ALL | QUOTE_NONNUMERIC | QUOTE_NONE`.
- Custom delimiters: TSV → `delimiter="\t"`.
- `csv.Sniffer().sniff(sample)` to auto-detect dialect.

### Big CSVs

```python
# stream line by line (preferred)
for row in csv.DictReader(open(...)): ...

# or pandas chunks
import pandas as pd
for chunk in pd.read_csv("big.csv", chunksize=100_000):
    process(chunk)
```

### Excel files

- `openpyxl` for `.xlsx`.
- `pandas.read_excel` / `to_excel`.
- For 1M+ rows, prefer CSV.

sections.title: 6. Binary files
sections.body:
```python
with open("img.png", "rb") as f:
    header = f.read(8)             # b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
```

`struct` module to pack/unpack C structs:

```python
import struct
struct.pack(">I", 1024)            # big-endian unsigned int (4 bytes)
struct.unpack(">I", b"\x00\x00\x04\x00")     # (1024,)
```

Format chars: `b/B` byte, `h/H` short, `i/I` int, `q/Q` long long, `f` float, `d` double, `s` string. Prefix `<` little-endian, `>` big-endian.

sections.title: 7. pathlib (modern, prefer over os.path)
sections.body:
```python
from pathlib import Path

p = Path("data") / "file.txt"
p.exists(); p.is_file(); p.is_dir()
p.suffix; p.stem; p.name; p.parent; p.parents
p.absolute(); p.resolve()
p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
p.write_text("hi", encoding="utf-8")
p.read_bytes(); p.write_bytes(b"...")
p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
p.unlink(missing_ok=True)              # delete file
p.rename(new); p.replace(new)          # atomic on same fs

for f in Path(".").rglob("*.py"): ...
for f in Path(".").iterdir(): ...
```

`pathlib` advantages:

- OS-aware (`PurePath` / `WindowsPath` / `PosixPath`).
- `/` operator concatenates paths.
- Methods replace many `os.path` calls.
- Returns `Path` objects with rich API.

sections.title: 8. Other formats (must know)
sections.body:
| Format  | Module                                  | Notes                                                   |
| ------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| INI     | `configparser`                          | simple key=value                                        |
| YAML    | `pyyaml` (3rd-party)                    | human-friendly                                          |
| TOML    | `tomllib` (3.11+ read), `tomli_w` write | `pyproject.toml`                                        |
| Pickle  | `pickle`                                | Python objects; **never unpickle untrusted data — RCE** |
| Shelve  | `shelve`                                | dict on disk via pickle                                 |
| SQLite  | `sqlite3`                               | embedded SQL DB; great for small apps                   |
| HDF5    | `h5py`, `tables`                        | big numeric data                                        |
| Parquet | `pyarrow`, `pandas`                     | columnar analytics                                      |
| XML     | `xml.etree.ElementTree`, `lxml`         | careful with XXE attacks                                |

sections.title: 9. Atomic / safe writes
sections.body:
Crash anywhere should never leave a half-written file:

```python
import os, tempfile
def atomic_write(path, data, encoding="utf-8"):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)) or "."
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding=encoding) as f:
            f.write(data); f.flush(); os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)              # atomic rename on same fs
    except Exception:
        os.unlink(tmp); raise
```

sections.title: 10. File locking (cross-process)
sections.body:
- Unix: `fcntl.flock`.
- Windows: `msvcrt.locking`.
- Cross-platform: `portalocker` library.

For a single process with threads, use `threading.Lock`.

sections.title: 11. Temporary files
sections.body:
```python
import tempfile
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", delete=False, suffix=".txt") as t:
    t.write("hi"); name = t.name

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    ...                                   # auto-deleted on exit
```

sections.title: 12. Best practices summary
sections.body:
- Always `with` + always specify `encoding`.
- Stream large files; never `f.read()` a 5 GB log.
- Catch specific errors: `FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError`, `IsADirectoryError`.
- Use `pathlib` for new code.
- Atomic writes for important data.
- Validate JSON/CSV at the boundary (Pydantic).
